title: Autonomous Lindblad Realizability of Nonunitary Linear Dynamics with a Carleman Lattice Boltzmann Application
abstract: Carleman lifting converts nonlinear polynomial dynamics into finite linear systems, but the resulting truncations are generally nonunitary and need not correspond to physical quantum evolution. We prove that a finite linear endpoint admits an autonomous Gorini--Kossakowski--Sudarshan--Lindblad (GKSL) realization on vacuum coherences if and only if it is invertible and power bounded. The construction is explicit and realizes the nonunitary map directly as open-system dynamics, with no endpoint postselection and with one encoding and one decoding over repeated timesteps. We apply the result to the complete D2Q9 multiple-relaxation-time lattice Boltzmann (LB) timestep by compiling collision and periodic streaming into a single Carleman endpoint. The resulting GKSL evolution reproduces the classical Carleman trajectory over multiple timesteps, while the remaining discrepancy from nonlinear LB dynamics is the expected Carleman truncation error. The result establishes a general criterion for autonomous open-quantum realization of finite nonunitary dynamics, with Carleman--LB dynamics as a concrete example.
summary: The paper develops a general criterion proving that any finite linear dynamic endpoint can be realized as an autonomous Lindblad evolution if the endpoint is invertible and power bounded. This theory is rigorously applied to the Lattice Boltzmann Method, successfully mapping its complex, dissipative timestep into a time-independent quantum master equation form.
main_problem: The central problem is establishing a general, necessary, and sufficient criterion for realizing finite linear dynamics (endpoints) derived from classical systems as an autonomous Gorini–Kossakowski–Sudarshan–Lindblad (GKSL) evolution in open quantum systems.
main_result: A finite real linear endpoint matrix A admits such an autonomous GKSL realization if and only if A is invertible and power bounded. This criterion was successfully applied to the D2Q9 Lattice Boltzmann Method timestep.
method: The authors combine Carleman linearization (to map nonlinear dynamics to a linear endpoint) with open quantum system theory, constructing the required Hamiltonian and Lindblad operators based on the properties of this endpoint matrix.
model_or_system: The study models nonunitary linear dynamics derived from classical fluid simulations, specifically applying the framework to the D2Q9 multiple-relaxation-time Lattice Boltzmann (LB) collision and streaming timestep.
key_observables: Invertibility and power boundedness of the endpoint matrix A; residual errors in physical identities (e.g., Kraus completeness); comparison between decoded quantum state and classical trajectory over time steps.

main_assumptions: The construction assumes that the dynamics can be accurately captured by a finite-dimensional linear endpoint derived from polynomial expansion, and it avoids postselection inherent to unitary embeddings.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the spectrum of the global endpoint matrix and plot the measured truncation error against time steps, demonstrating expected cubic scaling consistent with the order of approximation.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the general mathematical framework (Theorem 4) linking GKSL realizability to endpoint properties. It then applies this theory by analyzing the D2Q9 LBM timestep, showing how collision and streaming are compiled into a single admissible endpoint for autonomous quantum evolution.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful bridge between classical computational physics (like Lattice Boltzmann) and rigorous open quantum system descriptions, offering a concrete method to treat dissipative nonunitary dynamics quantum mechanically without resorting to measurement postulates.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Left: spectrum of the global endpoint A2 on the 3 × 3 periodic lattice against the unit circle. The 9 unit-modulus eigenvalues are neutral Carleman modes, including conserved modes and degree-two product modes, and are all semisimple, which is what makes the endpoint power bounded. The right panel shows the eigenvalues of the damping matrix Γ of the compiled generator, which are nonnegative up to floating-point roundoff. The neutral directions correspond to the unit-modulus eigenvalues shown in the left panel.

FIG. 2. Truncation error against the nonlinear reference after 10 timesteps, with a cubic reference line. The measured slope follows the cubic prediction, consistent with the leading truncation error arising from omitted degree-three terms rather than from the GKSL realization.
